welcome.lockedBinBody: Set up storage first — the bin has to live inside a container you have approved.
welcome.lockedAlertsBody: Set up email first — an alert nobody receives reads as nothing having happened.
welcome.heading: Let's set up your library
welcome.intro: A few things worth settling before anything else. Every one of them is a Control panel page too, so nothing here is your only chance to answer it — and you can leave at any point.
welcome.storageIntro: Two folders, and nothing else works without them: somewhere to keep the covers and previews the app generates, and at least one folder your libraries are allowed to read.
welcome.storagePathNote: Both are paths as the server sees them. In Docker that means the path inside the container — /media, not /mnt/user/media.
welcome.containersNote: A container is a folder you are approving. Libraries can then use it or anything inside it — a mistyped path can't wander off into the rest of the disk.
welcome.thumbnailSaveFailed: Unable to save the thumbnail path
welcome.binIntro: Deleting from the app moves files to the Recycle Bin rather than erasing them. By default each library keeps its own hidden .trash folder — instant to delete into, since nothing leaves the disk it was already on.
welcome.binNote: One folder for everything is worth choosing if anything else reads the same shares. Immich, a backup job or a sync client will happily index a library's .trash and go on showing everything you deleted as though it were still there.
welcome.binBrowseLocked: The bin already holds items — empty it before moving it
welcome.binPathNote: Best decided now: once anything is in the bin, the location can only change while it is completely empty. Keep it on the same disk as your libraries — across disks, deleting copies every byte instead of being a rename.
welcome.binSaveFailed: Unable to save the Recycle Bin location
welcome.binPickerIntro: Choose a folder inside an approved container — one outside every library, since anything inside a library is scanned.
welcome.backupHeading: A copy to go back to
welcome.backupIntro: A nightly archive of everything the app knows but your files do not: the catalogue, who has access, what everyone has read and listened to, and every setting on this page. Rebuilt from your media alone, none of that comes back.
welcome.backupNote: Not the media itself — that is far larger and already sitting in your libraries. A backup is small, which is why it can run every night.
welcome.backupToggle: Back up automatically, once a day
welcome.backupPathNote: Archives are written to {{path}}. Worth copying somewhere off this machine as well — a backup on the same disk as the thing it is backing up survives a mistake, but not a failed drive.
welcome.backupSavedDaily: Backing up daily at {{time}}, keeping the last {{count}}.
welcome.backupSavedMore: Change it any time in Control panel → Maintenance → Backup, where you can also make one now or restore from one.
welcome.backupSaveFailed: Unable to save the backup schedule
welcome.alertsIntro: The app can write to you when an account signs in from a network it has not seen before — the earliest sign that a password has been guessed, phished or reused.
welcome.alertsToggle: Email me about sign-ins from a new network
welcome.alertsTestNote: Worth sending yourself a test on the previous step first — an alert that cannot arrive reads exactly like nothing having happened.
welcome.alertsSavedBody: Change it any time in Control panel → Security.
welcome.alertsSaveFailed: Unable to save the alert setting
welcome.emailIntro: Optional, and worth doing: two-factor codes, invite links, security alerts and Send to e-reader all travel this way. Without it they simply never arrive.
welcome.passwordStored: Stored — leave blank to keep it
welcome.sendTestHint: Send yourself a test to prove it works.
welcome.testSentBody: Check {{email}}. If it arrived, email works — and the next step can put it to use.
welcome.mailSaveFailed: Unable to save the email settings
welcome.testSendFailed: Unable to send the test email
welcome.themeIntro: The look the sign-in screen uses, and what a new member starts with. Everyone can change their own afterwards in their profile.
